p_ovr_faq_description: All information you may need regarding voting by absentee ballot for elections in Iowa. You will need to submit an Absentee Ballot Request Form to your county auditor. Click the button directly below to pull up a PDF of the form to print out.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_request_title: How to Request an Absentee Ballot
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_request_form: To vote by absentee ballot in Iowa, a registered voter may make written application to their County Auditor for an absentee ballot. A written application for a mailed absentee ballot must be received by the voter's County Auditor no later than 5:00 p.m. 15 days before the election.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_request_form_p: In order to receive an absentee ballot, a registered voter MUST provide the following necessary information:
p_ovr_faq_voter_verification_option_driv: Iowa Driver's License or Non-Operator ID Number
p_ovr_faq_voter_verification_option_vote: Four digit Voter PIN located on the voter's Iowa Voter ID Card
p_ovr_faq_voter_verification_option_requ: Any voter may request an Iowa Voter ID Card by contacting their County Auditor's Office
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_request_requir: The name OR date of the election for which you are requesting an absentee ballot
Party affiliation - only required for Primary Elections, which are held in even numbered years
Signature and date the form was completed
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_request_recomm: All voters are encouraged to provide their phone number and/or email address in the event their County Auditor needs to confirm any information on the request form.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_descr: Registered voters may request an absentee ballot to be sent to them by mail. You must complete an absentee ballot request form and return the original, signed form to your county auditor. The request form does not need to be witnessed or notarized. A written application for a mailed absentee ballot must be received by the voter's County Auditor no later than 5:00 p.m. 15 days before the election.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_age: Someone who will be 18 years old by the date of an upcoming election may request an absentee ballot if he or she is pre-registered to vote.
p_no_locations_found_for_this_election: No locations found for this election
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_quest: If you have questions about absentee voting, please contact your County Auditor.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_deadl: The request form must be received in the county auditor's office by 5 p.m. 15 days before the election. If the request is received so late that it is unlikely the absentee ballot can be returned by mail in time to be considered for counting, the county auditor will enclose a statement to that effect with the absentee ballot.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_recei: After receiving a request form, the county auditor will mail the voter a ballot. With the ballot, the county auditor will include instructions on how to mark the ballot as well as how to return the ballot.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_retur: You can return your voted absentee ballot by mail. Absentee ballots received in the county auditor's office by the time the polls close on election day are eligible for counting. Read the instructions sent with the ballot.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_ballot_req_mail_deliv: You can return your voted absentee ballot by mail. Absentee ballots received in the county auditor's office by the time the polls close on election day are eligible for counting. Read the instructions sent with the ballot.
Deliver your voted absentee ballot to the county auditor's office before the polls close on election day,
Surrender your voted absentee ballot at the polls and vote a regular ballot, or
Vote a provisional ballot at the polls if you cannot surrender your voted absentee ballot.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_instructions: Mark your ballot, and then follow the instructions included with your ballot to return it in the postage-paid return envelope. It is vital that you utilize the return envelope supplied by the county auditor.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_option_mail: Mail your ballot so that is received before 8 PM CT on Election Day
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_option_hand_d: Hand deliver your ballot to your county auditor during business hours or any time up until 8 PM CT on Election Day.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_option_design: Hand deliver your ballot to your county auditor during business hours or any time up until 8 PM CT on Election Day.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_designee_fami: The designee is an immediate family member.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_designee_hous: The designee is a member of your household.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_designee_disa: You are disabled and you have designated someone to return your ballot.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_directions: Directions and rules for designating someone to return your ballot are included in the official instructions included with your mailed ballot.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_surrender_bal: Surrender your absentee ballot at your precinct polling place on Election Day and vote a regular ballot
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_proviional_ba: Vote a provisional ballot at the polls on Election Day if you cannot surrender your voted absentee ballot.
p_ovr_faq_returning_ballot_additional_in: Voted absentee ballots cannot be delivered to the polling place on Election Day - only to your county auditor's office.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_alternatives_title: Can I vote Absentee in other ways besides mailing?
p_ovr_faq_absentee_alternatives_in_perso:
You may cast an absentee ballot in person at your county auditor's office before any election.
You must vote your absentee ballot at the auditor's office. You cannot take the ballot home with you. For voters who need assistance in marking their ballots, an accessible ballot marking device is available at the county auditor's office.

For primary and general elections, absentee ballots will be available no earlier than 20 days at the county auditors' offices. For all other elections, ballots will be available as soon as they are ready, but not sooner than 20 days before an election.

In-person absentee voting is not available on election day at the auditor's office unless the polls open at noon. If the polls open at noon, you may cast an absentee ballot at the county auditor's office from 8 a.m. to 11 a.m. on election day.
p_ovr_faq_absentee_alternatives_satellit: Satellite absentee voting stations provide in-person absentee voting at locations other than the auditor's office. You must mark the absentee ballot at the satellite station and leave it with the officials. You cannot take the ballot home with you.
All satellite stations must be accessible to people with disabilities. To find out whether a satellite station is planned for an election, contact your county auditor.

You may request a satellite station by filing a petition with the county auditor. The petition must contain signatures of at least 100 eligible electors living in the jurisdiction. The petition must be filed with the county auditor conducting the election by the filing deadlines listed in §53.11, which varies by election type.

NOTICE TO VOTERS: Your polling place may have changed. Please visit this website before each election to check for updated information.
County Auditor must finalize polling places by 20 days before the election, but polling place locations could change due to an emergency.

*The polling place data on this page is for regularly scheduled Primary, General, and City/School Elections only.
*It is provided by county auditors through the statewide voter registration database.
*For Special Elections, please confirm the polling place hours and location with the as the locations may have been consolidated or vote centers may be used.
*For all elections, the polls will be open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m.
*If you have concerns or questions about your polling place or voter registration please contact your County Auditor.
*If you have moved to Iowa from another State or to a different county in Iowa, pre-register to vote in your new county before the first election in which you wish to vote.
*If you registered after or missed the pre-registration deadline, Election-pay-Registration is available.
*If you are 17 years old you may participate in a primary election if you will be 18 on or before the day of the corresponding regular election. For all other elections you must be 18 years old on or before election day.
*Secretary of State does not guarantee the accuracy of the locations as mapped by Google and Bing.

Deadline Alert: {{registrationDeadline}} is the last day to register before the {{electionDate}} election.

If you are not a U.S. citizen and a resident of Pennsylvania at least 30 days before the next election, you CANNOT register to vote.

If you have any questions, please call 1.877.VOTESPA (1.877.868.3772).

p_submit_application_message:
To vote in the next election, you must complete your application by {{registrationDeadline}}. You can submit your application:
  • On this web site
  • Delivered to your county voter registration office
  • By mail to your county voter registration office, received by {{registrationDeadline}}
p_additional_info_message:
Click here to download a blank voter registration form

If you are on active duty in the military, or you are a hospitalized or bedridden veteran, you can register at any time. See www.fvap.gov for more information.

If you have one, please have your PA driver's license or PennDOT ID available to reference as you complete the application.

Also, please know any section or field that's marked with a red indicator or an asterisk (*) is required to be filled out in order to submit an application.

Please avoid the use of 'Autofill' features when completing your application.

Frequently Asked Questions
